free_tier.stated: FOSSVPS is a free 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 64 GiB VPS gated on a human review of the applicant's open-source work. The provider's own forum posts show a second gate: forum reputation on named boards, with entire communities excluded. 'Nodeseek is no longer an accepted forum for potential new clients. Clients with good non spammy reputations are only accepted from LET or LES. Registration via a VPN is blocked. Throw away email addresses are blocked. Registering from Russia, China or North Korea is blocked.' And on the abuse that caused it: '29th of May VPS's belonging to NodeSeek clients will be terminated with no records kept.'

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The per-node sponsor dates are the composition rule: a box on buc2 expired 2026-10-17 and a rebuild to another node destroys the data, so this is a place to run a workload and not a place to keep state.

limits.value: The gate is a reputation held on one of two named forums plus a country the operator will accept, so an applicant with no LET or LES history and a blocked country cannot enter at all, whatever their open-source work.

notes: First, the identity cost is not merely an open-source track record: it is a reputation on one of two forums, which is an institutional standing a user does not hold, so the verdict moves from qualifies-with-caveat to fails-identity. Second, the node list carries printed end dates and the nearest ones are in the past or within weeks: buc2 ended 2026-10-17 and buc1 ended 2026-04-17, which is why the 64 GiB machine is a recurring rebuild rather than an allocation. The country exclusions are recorded here as a reachability fact about who the operator serves, not as a judgement. qualifies-with-caveat via a07-regional. The one recorded is the better-evidenced.
